title: “Apples, Peaches, Pumpkin Pie” by Jay & the Techniques
text: "Apples, Peaches, Pumpkin Pie" is a 1967 song written by Maurice Irby, Jr. and first released by Sam the Sham and The Pharaohs in November 1966 as "Ready or Not".

title: “Incense and Peppermints” by Strawberry Alarm Clock
text: "Incense and Peppermints" is a 1967 song by the American psychedelic rock band Strawberry Alarm Clock. The song is officially credited as having been written by John S. Carter and Tim Gilbert, although it was based on an instrumental idea by band members Mark Weitz and Ed King.

title: “Ruby Tuesday” by The Rolling Stones
text: "Ruby Tuesday" is a song by the English rock band the Rolling Stones, released in January 1967. The song became the band's fourth number-one hit in the United States and reached number three in the United Kingdom as a double A-side with "Let's Spend the Night Together".

title: Mr. Dressup
text: Mr. Dressup is a Canadian children's television series, starring Ernie Coombs, a former understudy of Fred Rogers, in the title role.

title: O'Keefe Centre Presents
text: O'Keefe Centre Presents is a series of Canadian variety specials that aired on CBC Television from 1967 to 1968.

title: Man Alive
text: Man Alive is a Canadian television program exploring faith and spirituality. The program premiered in 1967 on CBC Television.

title: The Pig and Whistle
text: The Pig and Whistle is a Canadian musical variety show that aired on the CTV television network from 1967 to 1977. Filmed in Toronto, Ontario but set in a fictional English pub, the show featured an assortment of Canadian, British and Irish performers.
